newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada June wage settlements average 1.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada June wage settlements average 1.8 pct.

text.p: Annual wage increases in Canadian collective bargaining agreements reached in June averaged 1.8 percent, up from a revised 1.4 percent (1.6 percent) in May, the Department of Human Resources Development said on Tuesday.
For the first half of 1997, annual wage increases in Canadian collective agreements averaged 1.7 percent, up from average adjustments of 0.9 percent for the years 1995 and 1996, the department said.
In the private sector, wages increased an average of 2.4 percent for 184,305 employees in 78 settlements.
"A clear, though modest, uptrend has emerged in the size of wage adjustments in the private sector," the department said in a statement.
In the public sector, wage increases averaged 0.9 percent of 163,435 employees in 106 settlements.

Wage increases are the average annual percentage increase in base rates -- the wage rate of the lowest paid classification in a bargaining unit -- over the term of the agreement in settlements negotiated during the period shown.
(For more information on the settlements, contact Human Resources Development's Workplace Information Directorate, at 1-800-567-6866 or 819-997-3117.)
